overview: All-Star Movies is one of Disney's three original Value resorts. Buildings are grouped by film, with giant movie icons towering over the courtyards, so it's colorful and fun for kids without a deluxe price tag.
suits: Families on a budget who plan to spend most of each day in the parks and just need a clean, cheerful place to sleep.
rooms:
Standard rooms are compact and sleep up to four, with two queen beds or one queen plus a pull-down bed in refreshed rooms. Check the latest room setup when you book.

Preferred rooms sit closer to the main building and food court, which saves a lot of walking.
pools: The main pool is the Fantasia Pool, with a smaller Duck Pond Pool nearby. Both have the same playful, oversized theming as the rest of the resort.
dining: Dining is the World Premiere Food Court, with grab-and-go items and a bar by the pool. There's no table-service restaurant on site.
gettingAround: Every park is reached by Disney bus. Plan extra time at busy times of day.
pros: One of the lowest-priced Disney-owned hotels
You still get Disney resort perks such as Early Theme Park Entry
cons: Buses are the only Disney transportation
Rooms are simple and on the small side
tips: Request a Preferred room or a building near the main building if you don't want a long walk.
Mobile order breakfast from the food court before you head to the bus.
Take a look at the other two All-Star resorts next door; they're within walking distance.
bestFor: Budget-minded families who'll spend all day in the parks.
